title: MERFISH zebrin share did not clearly predict cerebellar firing rates across or within lobules in 40 behaving IBL mice; zebrin-group rate ratios (0.90-0.96) were above the 0.64 reported at rest
abstract: Zhou et al. 2014 reported that zebrin-negative (Z-) Purkinje cells (PCs) in awake resting mice fire simple spikes faster than zebrin-positive (Z+) PCs (Z+/Z- rate ratio about 0.64). We tested this structure-function link in IBL Brain-Wide Map units of behaving mice (4,839 good cerebellar-cortex units, 40 mice, 11 labs). We took the zebrin map from Allen MERFISH PCs of two brains: supertype Gaba_1 is Aldoc-high/Plcb4-low (Z+) and Gaba_2 is Aldoc-low/Plcb4-high (Z-). Under a plan frozen before any zebrin-rate computation, the lobule Z+ share had a negative but uncertain rank correlation with the median rate of units at 20 Hz or more (rho -0.32, 95% mouse-bootstrap CI -0.69 to +0.12, 14 lobules; Zhuang map -0.34). The local Z+ share inside lobules varied too little (SD 0.044) to test stripes, and its slope was not different from 0. Exploratory: lobules rich in Z+ PCs had fewer very fast units (95th-percentile rho -0.56, CI -0.75 to -0.11). But for Z+ dominated lobules (NOD, FL, PFL, UVU) against Z- dominated lobules (CENT2, CENT3, SIM), the median-rate ratio was 0.90 (0.76 to 1.06) for units at 20 Hz or more and 0.955 (0.78 to 1.17) for an ACG-defined PC-like class. Both intervals exclude 0.64. PC-like units fired 1.32 times faster (1.15 to 1.48) in hemisphere than in vermis lobules. Limitations: no cell-type ground truth (the unit sets mix PCs with other cells), whole-session rates mix task and rest, single-brain MERFISH maps with about 100-200 um registration error, few mice in Z+ lobules, and the group contrasts were defined after the primary output. IBL-derived tables, code, statistics and figures are included; Allen-derived values are regenerated by script.

display.caption: Median firing rate per cerebellar lobule with 95% mouse-bootstrap bars. (a) Good units at 20 Hz or more (pre-registered unit set). (b) PC-like units (exploratory ACG class). Lobules are ordered from Z- dominated (orange) to Z+ dominated (blue) by MERFISH zebrin share; circles are vermis and squares are hemisphere lobules. Tick labels give units and mice.

Effect summary with 95% mouse-bootstrap intervals. (a) Rate ratios: pre-registered within-lobule effect (z=1 against z=0, an extrapolation because z varies little in lobules), Z+/Z- lobule-group ratios, the PC-like share ratio and the hemisphere/vermis ratio. The dashed line is the 0.64 ratio of Zhou et al. 2014. (b) Spearman rho of lobule Z+ share against lobule rate for the pre-registered H1 and its variants.

Cumulative firing-rate distributions of (a) all good units and (b) PC-like units in Z- dominated (CENT2, CENT3, SIM), mixed and Z+ dominated (NOD, FL, PFL, UVU) lobules. The Z- group has more fast units overall, but PC-like rate distributions are similar.

citations.reason: Zhou et al. 2014 reported the Z-/Z+ simple-spike rate difference in awake resting mice that we test in behaving mice.
